question: Can the selected real plus-recessive direction's finite two-sided Qswitch kappa-sensitivity box be transported to a finite two-sided projective h(Q0)=partial_kappa rho(Q0) enclosure by adjoining only J_Q=-U^2, without constructing Y pointwise or differentiating the Gamma_1 tail?
primary_sources: Selection context inherited through the pinned upstream results: NIST DLMF section 2.7(iii), Liouville-Green approximation for the selected real plus-recessive family: https://dlmf.nist.gov/2.7#iii

declared_conventions.auxiliary_integral_state: J_Q=-U^2 and J(Qswitch)=0, so J(Q0)=integral_Q0^Qswitch U(Q)^2 dQ
declared_conventions.execution: hash-pinned interval-Taylor coefficient/whole-step majorants with one added exact J jet; no Bessel evaluation, black-box ODE integration, quadrature, root solve, finite difference, sampling, kernel panel or bisection

method_reuse.used_for: coefficient derivatives, full-step majorants and outward interval helpers only

upstream_results.role: supplies the same selected-family finite two-sided p_switch=-h(Qswitch) box and its full-strip provenance
pins the exact corridor, selected switch rho seed, switch normalization and nonzero Q0 chart only; Gamma_1 face signs are unused
supplies an independently derived one-sided endpoint sign margin used only as a consistency check

assumptions: The hash-pinned Qswitch p and rho boxes refer to the same selected real plus-recessive projective family on the same exact closed K times Lambda strip; losing their parameter correlation by taking a product box is conservative.
Switch normalization U(Qswitch)=1 is finite and kappa-dependent normalization is fixed separately at each parameter, so Y(Qswitch)=0 and W(Qswitch)=p_switch.
The regular finite U IVP and the scalar J equation can be propagated backward from Qswitch to Q0 by full-box interval Taylor steps.
Only U(Q0), not U on the open leg, is divided by. Intermediate U zeros would not obstruct the regular U,J flow or Wronskian identity.
The resulting switch-normalized U and J boxes are auxiliary; only h(Q0) is scale invariant.
